excerpt: Scratchpad is a faster interface to Salesforce for sales teams: pipeline sheets, bulk updates, deal changes and notes that save to Salesforce. $16–$20 per user a month.
content:
Scratchpad is a San Francisco software company that builds a workspace on top of Salesforce for sales teams. Instead of clicking through Salesforce pages, reps and managers work in Scratchpad's own views, and every change writes straight back to Salesforce, which stays the system of record. Its website lists spreadsheet-style and Kanban views of any Salesforce object, a view of what changed on each deal, bulk updates to fix missing next steps or stale close dates, free-form sales notes that save to the right opportunity, and a heads-up display and Chrome extension reachable with a keyboard shortcut from any tab. It connects through the Salesforce API and inherits each user's Salesforce permissions, and says it is SOC 2 Type 2 compliant.

Pouyan Salehi is co-founder and CEO. VentureBeat reported that he co-founded the company in 2019 with Cyrus Karbassiyoon; the two had previously co-founded the outbound sales startup PersistIQ.

Funding

Crunchbase News reported Scratchpad's $13 million Series A, led by Craft Ventures. In January 2022 Scratchpad announced a $33 million Series B, again led by Craft Ventures with Accel participating, bringing total funding to $49 million. At the time it said it had tens of thousands of users at thousands of companies, naming customers such as Algolia, Ironclad, Quora, Twilio, Udemy and Vanta.

Pricing

Scratchpad has one plan with every feature: $20 per user per month billed monthly, or $16 per user per month billed annually. New teams get a 30-day free trial with no feature limits.

Who it suits

It suits account executives, sales managers and RevOps teams who live in Salesforce and want faster pipeline updates and cleaner data. Teams on HubSpot or another CRM cannot use it, since it works only with Salesforce.

We have not tested Scratchpad. This page is based on Scratchpad's website, pricing page (checked 15 October 2026) and funding announcement, and on VentureBeat and Crunchbase News.
